title: Daily Market Digest: Inflation Fears Drive Tech Sell-Off
subtitle: October 15, 2026 - Market Close Summary (October 14) and Overnight/Pre-market (October 15)

items.headline: Tech Sector Plunges as Higher Inflation Fuels Rate Hike Concerns
items.summary: U.S. equities experienced their sharpest decline since July during Wednesday's session (October 14), largely driven by disappointing September inflation data that intensified fears of further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. The technology sector bore the brunt of the sell-off, particularly AI-linked shares, as investors weighed the prospects of increased borrowing costs. Pre-market indicators for Thursday (October 15) suggest continued pressure on tech stocks.

items.headline: Apple (AAPL) Crosses $5T Market Value
items.summary: Apple defied the broader market downturn, gaining 0.5% to close above a five-trillion-dollar market value for the first time amidst a tech sell-off.

items.headline: UnitedHealth Group Surges
items.summary: UnitedHealth Group ($UNH) was among the strongest performers, rising 4.86% as the broader market declined.

items.headline: Merck Posts Strong Gains
items.summary: Merck ($MRK) saw a significant increase, climbing 3.85% during Wednesday's trading session.

items.headline: CoreWeave Plunges Amid AI Financing Concerns
items.summary: Cloud provider CoreWeave lost 15% during Wednesday's session, with pre-market trading on Thursday seeing another 4.5% slip, as concerns intensified regarding the financing of debt-heavy AI infrastructure companies.

items.headline: Oracle Falls on Tech Weakness
items.summary: Oracle ($ORCL) declined 8.8% as technology shares slid following renewed inflation concerns.

items.headline: Dell Technologies Experiences Sharp Drop
items.summary: Dell Technologies ($DELL) experienced a significant downturn, plunging 11.2% in Wednesday's trading.

items.headline: Nvidia Leads Semiconductor Slide
items.summary: AI chip leader Nvidia ($NVDA) fell 3.2% on Wednesday and another 1.3% in pre-market trading, extending the semiconductor sector's losing streak.

items.headline: September CPI Exceeds Expectations, Ignites Rate Hike Fears
items.summary: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September rose 3.7% year-over-year, surpassing the 3.6% consensus forecast. Core inflation, excluding food and energy, also came in higher than anticipated at 2.6%. This data point has heightened expectations for potential Federal Reserve interest rate increases, with markets now pricing in about 40 basis points of Fed hikes by January and an October move edging up.

items.headline: Technology and Communication Services Lead Market Decline; Energy Continues to Outperform
items.summary: Eight of the S&P 500's eleven sectors declined on October 14, with Technology losing 2.6% and Communication Services falling 1.78%. The semiconductor index, a key component of the AI boom, dropped 4.3% for its sixth consecutive decline. In contrast, the S&P 500 Energy index remains the market's top-performing sector year-to-date, surging +46.34%.

items.headline: AI-Linked Shares Face Deepening Sell-Off Amid Debt Concerns
items.summary: A deepening sell-off in AI-linked shares hit global markets, extending from Wall Street to Asia. Concerns are mounting over the increasing cost of financing behind the AI infrastructure boom, with some market participants questioning the sustainability of debt-heavy AI companies.

items.headline: TSMC Reports Record Profit, Maintains Strong AI Demand Outlook
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) reported a record third-quarter net profit of NT$763.1 billion, a 69% increase year-over-year and exceeding analyst expectations. The company expressed confidence in continued strong AI demand despite the broader tech downturn.

items.headline: Mixed Bank Earnings Reports
items.summary: Major U.S. banks reported mixed third-quarter earnings. Bank of America sank after reporting weaker profits than analysts expected, while Marsh & McLennan Companies, Bank Of New York Mellon, and PNC reported earnings above expectations.
